final_proof:
Let $S_k = \set{i \in I : \paren{x_k}_i \ne 0}$ for each $k \in \closedint 1 m$. 
By the definition of the generalized Hilbert sequence space $H^\alpha$, each $S_k$ is a countable set.
Let $U = \bigcup_{k=1}^m S_k$. Since $U$ is the union of a finite number of countable sets, $U$ itself is a countable set.

Since $U$ is countable, there exists an injective mapping $f: U \to \N$, where \N = \set{0, 1, 2, \ldots}.
For each $k \in \closedint 1 m$, define a sequence $y_k = \sequence{\paren{y_k}_n}_{n=0}^\infty$ as follows:
$$ \paren{y_k}_n = \begin{cases} \paren{x_k}_{f^{-1}\paren{n}} & \text{if } n \in f\paren{U} \\ 0 & \text{if } n \notin f\paren{U} \end{cases} $$

First, we show that $y_k \in \ell^2$ for each $k$.
For any $k \in \closedint 1 m$, the non-zero terms of the sequence $y_k$ occur only at indices $n \in f\paren{S_k} \subseteq f\paren{U}$.
We can evaluate the sum of squares:
$$ \sum_{n=0}^\infty \paren{y_k}_n^2 = \sum_{n \in f\paren{U}} \paren{y_k}_n^2 = \sum_{n \in f\paren{U}} \paren{x_k}_{f^{-1}\paren{n}}^2 = \sum_{i \in U} \paren{x_k}_i^2 $$
Since $S_k \subseteq U$, for all $i \in I \setminus U$, we have \paren{x_k}_i = 0.
Thus, $\sum_{i \in U} \paren{x_k}_i^2 = \sum_{i \in I} \paren{x_k}_i^2$.
By the definition of $A$, this generalized sum is convergent, meaning the series $\sum_{n=0}^\infty \paren{y_k}_n^2$ is a convergent series of numbers. Therefore, $y_k \in \ell^2$.

Next, we show that for any $a, b \in \closedint 1 m$, $\map{d_{\ell^2}}{y_a, y_b} = \map{d_2}{x_a, x_b}$.
We have:
$$ \map{d_{\ell^2}}{y_a, y_b}^2 = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \paren{\paren{y_a}_n - \paren{y_b}_n}^2 $$
Since $\paren{y_a}_n = 0$ and $\paren{y_b}_n = 0$ for $n \notin f\paren{U}$, we can write:
$$ \sum_{n=0}^\infty \paren{\paren{y_a}_n - \paren{y_b}_n}^2 = \sum_{n \in f\paren{U}} \paren{\paren{x_a}_{f^{-1}\paren{n}} - \paren{x_b}_{f^{-1}\paren{n}}}^2 = \sum_{i \in U} \paren{\paren{x_a}_i - \paren{x_b}_i}^2 $$
Since $S_a \subseteq U$ and $S_b \subseteq U$, if $i \in I \setminus U$, then $\paren{x_a}_i = 0$ and $\paren{x_b}_i = 0$, so $\paren{x_a}_i - \paren{x_b}_i = 0$.
Thus, $\sum_{i \in U} \paren{\paren{x_a}_i - \paren{x_b}_i}^2 = \sum_{i \in I} \paren{\paren{x_a}_i - \paren{x_b}_i}^2 = \map{d_2}{x_a, x_b}^2$.
Taking the square root of both sides, we obtain $\map{d_{\ell^2}}{y_a, y_b} = \map{d_2}{x_a, x_b}$.

Finally, we show that $y_a \ne y_b \iff x_a \ne x_b$ for all $a, b \in \closedint 1 m$.
If $x_a = x_b$, then $\paren{x_a}_i = \paren{x_b}_i$ for all $i \in I$. For any $n \in \N$, if $n \in f\paren{U}$ then $i = f^{-1}\paren{n} \in U$, so $\paren{y_a}_n = \paren{x_a}_i = \paren{x_b}_i = \paren{y_b}_n$. If $n \notin f\paren{U}$, $\paren{y_a}_n = 0 = \paren{y_b}_n$. Hence $y_a = y_b$.
If $x_a \ne x_b$, there exists some $i \in I$ such that $\paren{x_a}_i \ne \paren{x_b}_i$. This implies that at least one of $\paren{x_a}_i$ or $\paren{x_b}_i$ is non-zero, so $i \in S_a \cup S_b \subseteq U$.
Then $n = f\paren{i} \in f\paren{U}$, and we have $\paren{y_a}_n = \paren{x_a}_i \ne \paren{x_b}_i = \paren{y_b}_n$. Thus $y_a \ne y_b$.
This completes the proof.
